ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, limited partners, and UBOs against: Public Safety Canada's Criminal Code schedule listing listed entities; OFAC SDN List and sectoral sanctions; UN Security Council Consolidated List; UK HMT sanctions (where applicable); FINTRAC guidance on politically exposed persons (domestic/foreign PEPs); Global Affairs Canada's Canadian Sanctions List; enhanced risk-identification and EDD for non-resident PEPs; screening language requirements where partner is a foreign jurisdiction

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Corporate Registry System / Alberta.ca Business Registry)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be filed in English and/or French in the proper Latin alphabet; Alberta's registry permits English/French names with statutory transliteration for diacritics; the name must be distinct from existing Alberta registered partnership, business corporation, or extra-provincial registrants; where a name contains numerals, symbols, or punctuation, must comply with name regulations and the Partnership Act; translation/transliteration of foreign-script names is required before search and reservation
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: words suggesting a public company if not incorporated
terms implying limited liability other than 'Limited Partnership'
words contrary to public interest as determined by the Registrar
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may submit a written request for reconsideration to the Registrar of Alberta Corporate Registry within 30 days of the rejection notice; the request must include the original NUANS-style search report or Alberta name search report, justification as to the distinctiveness of the proposed name, any supporting consent from affected parties, and the prescribed appeal form; if reconsideration fails, an administrative review can be filed in Alberta Court of King's Bench under the Business Corporations Act (or Partnership Act analog), or apply for a new name using a fresh search. The Registrar may provide a one-time name reservation extension if the initial 30-day reservation has not expired and good cause is shown; otherwise the applicant must submit a new name reservation request and pay the current filing fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For an Alberta Limited Partnership, a physical registered office within Alberta is required; virtual office services generally permissible only if a physical Canadian/Alberta address is provided and the registered agent can receive service of process; industry (digital design agency with no regulated license) is low-risk, so virtual registered office combined with a commercial substance address for banking is accepted; however, non-resident general partner situations increase documentary substance requirements and financial institutions generally insist on a physical operational nexus for Stripe and Wise underwriting
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk (<15%). Alberta registry does not routinely inspect LPs; but financial institution KYB, Merchant of Record underwriting, and CRA registration checks impose document-based verification; unannounced on-site inspection likelihood is approximately 8%, mainly triggered by AML red flags, tax residence disputes, or use of virtual office with non-resident general partner

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c P-3, ss 44, 50, 51(1), 52, 53(1), 56; registered limited partnerships are filed with the Alberta Corporate Registry rather than incorporated under the Business Corporations Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, Government of Alberta, through Registry Xpress or an authorized Alberta Registry Agent.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Limited Partnership in the prescribed form under the Partnership Act, Alberta.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for an Alberta limited partnership; limited partners may contribute cash, property, or services at agreed values, and no escrow or trust account is statutorily required for capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: We, the general partner of the Alberta limited partnership to be, resolve as follows: FIRST, the limited partnership accepts the capital contributions set out in Schedule A from each subscribing limited partner, at values as recorded. SECOND, the registered office and principal records place shall be [address], Alberta, and Service Alberta Corporate Registry is designated as the filings registry. THIRD, [Name of general partner] is appointed as the managing general partner, with full authority under the Partnership Act, and [Name of attorney] is appointed as attorney for service if required. FOURTH, the general partner is authorized to execute the Declaration of Limited Partnership, retain counsel and accountants, and establish banking and payment-rail accounts. This resolution is effective upon registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, via Registry Xpress or an authorized Registry Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name search request for the proposed limited partnership name in Alberta. The name must contain 'Limited Partnership', 'L.P.', or 'société en commandite' and must not create a confusing resemblance with an existing corporate or business name. Secure a name reservation before preparing the governing declaration.
required_dossiers: Name search request form or agent instruction
Entity identification details of the proposed general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried due to conflicting or reserved names, file a revised name request promptly with supporting explanation; the Registry Agent will re-run the search and release or modify the reservation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting the limited partnership agreement and statutory declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private legal counsel; notarization where a partner is a body corporate or an attorney executes on behalf of a non-resident partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft a complete limited partnership agreement addressing admission, capital accounts, profit sharing, dissolution, and general partner authority. Prepare the statutory Declaration of Limited Partnership containing the partnership name, Alberta registered office address, names and addresses of general partners, the maximum amount of capital contribution to be made by limited partners, and any prescribed particulars.
required_dossiers: General partner consent and authorization letter
Corporate resolution or certified certificate of status if the general partner is a body corporate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry notes defective particulars, prepare and file an amended Declaration of Limited Partnership correcting the deficiency before the registration certificate is issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing the Declaration of Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, Registry Xpress or physical counter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed Declaration of Limited Partnership, the name reservation, a completed Statement of Registered Office or head office address, and the applicable registration fee. Upon acceptance, the Registry will issue a Certificate of Registration confirming the limited partnership's creation and assigning an Alberta corporate access number or partnership registry number.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is queried for missing signatures, contact details, or corporate authorization, correct the form and resubmit through the Registry Agent within the prescribed cure period; obtain a stamped corrected receipt if the registration date is contested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency; Service Alberta for provincial tax registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the limited partnership for federal Business Number and GST/HST if taxable supplies exceed the small supplier threshold. Determine whether an Alberta income tax election or corporate partner notifications are required. Open a Canadian-dollar business bank account for the partnership and maintain partnership records at the registered address.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration for the limited partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or Alberta Revenue queries the partnership registration, submit the Certificate of Registration and partnership details electronically, correct the beneficial ownership information, and request a confirmation or employer account adjustment within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal business licence and premises clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipal licensing department where the Alberta registered office is situated, such as the City of Calgary or City of Edmonton
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a municipal business licence covering the interaction design subscription agency's physical premises, if any. Ensure the office premise meets local building occupancy, fire safety, and accessibility requirements. The limited partnership may operate as a registered virtual office with no industrial plant unless dedicated design workstations are established.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration of the limited partnership
Proof of address and lease or registered office consent
Fire and life safety compliance checklist for the premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality requires additional inspections, book the required inspection and supply corrected floor plans, leasehold permits, or lease renewal documents; otherwise update the registered address and resubmit the licence application.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No dedicated industrial licensing authority applies to a product interface design and digital design subscription agency in Alberta; municipal business licensing is administered by the local municipality.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory industrial operating or manufacturing permit is required for ISIC 7410 in Alberta; a municipal business licence may be required if the limited partnership maintains a physical office.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas, Environmental Assessment Program
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the registered activity is an office-based professional design service with no mandatory environmental impact assessment under the Environmental Assessment (Mandatory and Exempt Activities) Regulation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, or point-source emissions are generated by UI/UX design subscription services; general office waste shall be handled under municipal waste bylaws, and electronic waste shall be recycled through approved Alberta Recycling programs if applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Where a physical design office is opened, obtain a fire safety inspection and clearance from the municipal fire authority, comply with the Alberta Building Code and structural load requirements for the leased premises, and register with Alberta Occupational Health and Safety for the workforce. No special occupational clearance beyond standard OHS obligations applies to subscription-based design service delivery.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); registration and account services are available through the CRA Business Registration Online service and CRA My Business Account. Alberta has no separate provincial general sales tax authority or provincial sales tax registration for ordinary supplies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Obtain a CRA Business Number (BN) and the applicable program accounts. A foreign limited partnership carrying on business in Canada or required to register for GST/HST generally applies to the CRA for a BN and GST/HST account using Business Registration Online where eligible, or the CRA's prescribed registration process. Provide partnership legal name, formation jurisdiction and documents, Canadian business address or contact details, business activities, start date, partners and authorized representative information. A non-resident may need to contact the CRA directly if online registration is unavailable and may be required to provide security. GST/HST registration is generally required when the partnership is not a small supplier and makes taxable supplies in Canada; voluntary registration may be available. A BN is not a corporate income-tax TIN, and an LP generally does not obtain a separate income-tax account solely because it exists: partnership income is generally reported by partners. A T5013 partnership information return may be required under the CRA filing rules. Non-resident partners may require Canadian tax identification and applicable withholding or tax-return compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style check-the-box election for a Canadian limited partnership. A partnership is generally fiscally transparent for Canadian income-tax purposes, with income and losses allocated to partners under the Income Tax Act. Classification is determined under Canadian law and the partnership agreement and facts; there is no general election to treat the LP as a corporation or to elect hybrid-mismatch status. Specific statutory elections may apply to particular transactions but do not change the LP's general classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST); Alberta does not impose a general provincial sales tax. HST applies in participating provinces, subject to place-of-supply rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in worldwide taxable supplies (including zero-rated supplies) over a single calendar quarter or over four consecutive calendar quarters, subject to the statutory small-supplier tests and exceptions. Special rules apply to non-resident digital-economy suppliers and platform operators supplying Canadian consumers; the applicable registration regime depends on the supplier's facts and whether it carries on business in Canada.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not generally require real-time tax-authority invoice clearance, fiscal stamping, or mandatory nationwide e-invoicing APIs. GST registrants must issue invoices or receipts containing prescribed information when required and retain adequate books and records; electronic records are permitted if accessible and compliant with CRA record-keeping requirements.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Qualifying exported goods are generally zero-rated where the statutory conditions are met, including export from Canada and required supplier records. Certain services supplied to non-residents may be zero-rated under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act, but exclusions and conditions apply; a customer's non-residence alone does not establish zero-rating. Design and digital subscription services require a supply-by-supply analysis, including the recipient, place and manner of performance, connection to Canadian real property or tangible personal property, and any applicable excluded service category. Zero-rating is not the same as exemption; eligible registrants may generally claim input tax credits attributable to zero-rated supplies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export declaration and applicable Canadian customs export reporting evidence, where required
Bill of lading, airway bill, courier record, or other carrier evidence identifying the goods and destination
Commercial invoice, sales contract, and proof of delivery or export
Customer identity and residence evidence, service agreement, deliverables, and records substantiating the recipient and place of supply for exported services
Inward remittance or banking records where available and relevant; Canada does not impose a universal inward remittance certificate requirement for GST zero-rating
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada has no general statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for qualifying export proceeds. The supplier must substantiate zero-rating and retain supporting records; CRA may reassess GST, deny related input tax credits or refunds, and impose arrears interest and applicable late-filing or other penalties. False statements or omissions may attract penalties under the Excise Tax Act, including gross-negligence penalties, and serious cases may result in prosecution. Reassessments are subject to statutory limitation periods and exceptions, including those applicable to misrepresentation attributable to neglect, carelessness, wilful default, or fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), with foreign-exchange regulatory oversight by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and anti-money-laundering supervision by FINTRAC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a fully convertible floating currency for both current and capital account transactions, compliant with IMF Article VIII. There are no exchange control restrictions on profit remittances out of Alberta. Non-resident limited partners may repatriate distributable earnings subject to domestic withholding tax rules (generally Part XIII of the Income Tax Act), including a mandatory 25% withholding on passive income unless reduced by treaty, and to automated CRS/FATCA reporting. Foreign currency accounts may be held by residents and non-residents alike without Bank of Canada approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada does not impose any statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds. Export receipts may be retained in foreign currency, held in CAD, or freely converted through authorized financial intermediaries without reporting to OSFI, subject only to FINTRAC transaction reporting thresholds (large cash and wire reports).

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: High for inbound international client collections via Wise and Stripe, and medium for primary operational settlement. Legal constraints: Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), any entity holding or transmitting funds on behalf of Canadians must be registered as a Money Services Business (MSB) with FINTRAC. Wise is a registered MSB in Canada and provides CAD and USD clearing with local ACH and SWIFT routing. Stripe is likewise registered and acts as a payment facilitator, not a deposit-taking institution. True EMI (Electronic Money Institution) licensing is not recognized at the federal level in Canada; a foreign EMI operating from the EU or UK may not accept deposits from Canadian clients without MSB registration, and an Alberta LP using an offshore EMI as a core external Treasury platform may attract anti-avoidance and sanctions concerns. For low-value recurring subscription receipts, Wise and Stripe present the most cost-efficient inbound rail, while domestic Tier-1 bank accounts remain mandatory for larger capital movements and CRS/FATCA transparency.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For an Alberta Limited Partnership, the general partner(s) and any individual or entity owning more than 25% of the partnership must undergo customer due diligence. In practice, Canadian Tier-1 banks require an interview, which may be conducted remotely via video conference only after notarized and apostilled corporate documentation has been submitted. A wholly remote, document-only account opening is generally not available for a non-resident LP. A Canadian-resident general partner or a solicitor’s referral can significantly reduce the need for a physical visit. For a foreign general partner, a physical appointment at the bank’s Canadian branch (or at a Canadian embassy/consulate abroad when remote notarization is not accepted) is commonly mandated. The final compliance decision always requires a live human interview to verify the control chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partner domiciled in a sanctions-affected or high-risk jurisdiction (e.g., FATF grey list) or holding >25% of LP interests.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed FINTRAC Large Cash/Financing EDD form; passport and secondary valid government-issued ID; notarized proof of residential address (utility bill plus bank letter); certified corporate registry extract for any legal entity partner; source of wealth summary with last two years' tax returns, audited financials, or business bank statements; PEP status confirmation and, if applicable, a clear PEP rationale; latest sanctions screening result from a credible commercial provider; written authority from the compliance officer for enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: LP structure obscures beneficial ownership through multiple tiers, nomination arrangements, or discretionary trust holdings.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed partnership agreement and all amendments; register of limited partners showing membership percentages and agreed capital commitments; beneficial ownership schedule for each partner through the legal chain to natural persons; unredacted trust deed or family arrangement when any interest is held via a trust; CFCA (Canadian Financial and Commercial Fraud Authority) form where applicable; T5013 (partnership information return) and annual partnership filing confirmations; written explanation of the LP's commercial purpose and how the control chain matches the bank's onboarding system.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large or one-off inbound capital injection (> CAD 100,000) from a foreign jurisdiction without a clearly documented business nexus to the design subscription business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board/Partner resolution authorising the capital contribution; signed capital commitment schedule from the partnership agreement; source of funds evidence (prior 12-month bank statements, liquid asset statements, or signed sale agreement); applicable tax residency certificate and FATCA/W-8BEN-E in case of US remitter; detailed wire purpose code and remittance narrative in Field 70 of the SWIFT MT103; pre-notification to the relationship manager with the expected sender name, account number, and approximate value; subscriber contract or engagement letter from the UI/UX platform aligning the funding to ongoing operational need.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For all inbound capital contributions, use SWIFT MT103 wires to the LP’s CBDC (Canadian domestic) account held at a Tier-1 bank. Field 50K (ordering customer) must exactly match the banking registry and partnership agreement; Field 59 must contain the legal name ‘ALBERTA UI UX DESIGN LP’ and its CA-AB account number. In Field 70, include the purpose code ‘CAPITAL_CONTRIBUTION’ and a continuous compliance reference number. For US-domiciled partners, use Fedwire/ACH via the bank’s US banking pass-through network to eliminate double FX. When the transfer originates in a non-CAD currency, attach a payment schedule and FX quotation from the beneficiary bank; for USD, route via the bank’s reciprocal ‘USD Clear’ facility. Verification procedures include: match sender name and account with prior notification; confirm the payer is an authorised partner or lender; run sanctions and negative-list screening; capture transfer details for FINTRAC and automatically create the CRS/FATCA record.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rail for trade settlements is SWIFT MT103 for cross-border payments to overseas contractors, licensing fees, or operating expenses. For recurring platform subscription and vendor payments, Wise is the most efficient rail, supporting low-value multi-currency conversion with open-market FX rates within registered MSB limits. For high-value or documentary settlements (e.g., design IP acquisition or equipment leases), a Commercial Letter of Credit (LC) or a Bank Payment Undertaking may be established through a Tier-1 Canadian bank; however, due to the services nature of ISIC 7410, LCs are not routinely used. Domestic CAD disbursements follow Interac e-Transfer for micro-transactions and EFT/ACH for payroll and supplier payments. For USD payments to US residents, the bank’s continental automated clearing house mirror is preferred, or a SWIFT MT103 if the counterparty is outside North America. Every outbound transfer must contain the appropriate MFIP/ISO purpose code (e.g., ‘BGBB’ for business disbursements or ‘BOSL’ for operating services) and be mirrored in the LP’s Treasury ledger for regulatory reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Call/put FX options on CAD/USD and CAD/EUR

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative dissolution after 60 days of delinquency

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory independent audit for private Limited Partnerships; audit required only for public companies or specific thresholds

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual confirmation of shareholding and UBO details required with Annual Return filing

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at partnership level (pass-through entity); income flows through to partners
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: None at LP level; partners may claim federal R&D tax credits (up to 35% refundable) and other deductions

tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Six months after the end of the fiscal year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue from UI/UX design subscriptions, digital services and related activities
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report allocable share of income to non-resident partners; no separate withholding tax on LP distributions

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business expenses including salaries, rent, marketing and professional fees
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must confirm economic substance; losses and deductions flow through to individual T1 returns

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership net income after allowable deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents receive K-1 equivalent statements for allocation; no TRC required for standard distributions

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: CAD 50 per day late filing penalty (maximum CAD 2,500); non-filing penalties up to CAD 100 per day after notice

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: N/A - Limited Partnerships are pass-through entities; no corporate-level withholding tax applies to distributions to partners
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: No DTA relief required for LP distributions; partners report income directly on personal T1 returns; no TRC submission required for ordinary distributions
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 10% statutory rate under ITA s.212(1), reduced to 0-5% under applicable tax treaties (e.g. 0% with US, UK); Interest: 25% statutory rate, reduced under treaties (e.g. 0% with many jurisdictions)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 50,000,000 for Master File / CbCR requirements; contemporaneous documentation recommended for significant related-party transactions
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Not applicable; Canada applies General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and economic substance principles under ITA s.245

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission or misrepresentation of partnership income on T2125
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction under Income Tax Act; fines up to CAD 5 million and imprisonment up to 5 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Partners and designated representatives face personal liability for unpaid taxes and can be subject to director liability provisions

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using LP solely for tax deferral without carrying on business in Alberta
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of transactions, denial of deductions and GAAR penalties up to 10 times the tax benefit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Partners may be assessed personally for tax; veil piercing does not apply to partnerships but personal assessments possible

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file suspicious transaction reports or maintain proper KYC for cross-border design subscriptions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to CAD 10 million under Proceeds of Crime Act; criminal charges possible
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individual partners and officers face personal fines, imprisonment and potential travel bans
